sideEffects.e: **Tolerance, dependence** and a withdrawal syndrome when stopped

pearls: Only the **levo enantiomer** carries the μ-agonist activity; the dextro form is a weak μ agonist and an NMDA antagonist (being developed for depression).
Works best inside a **structured program** with random urine screens and psychosocial support; tapering straight to abstinence rarely succeeds long term.
**Injecting** the buprenorphine–naloxone combination gives no high and may precipitate withdrawal, so it blocks diversion of the sublingual form.
Like methadone, most successful in a **structured maintenance program** (random urine screens, psychosocial services); tapering to abstinence rarely succeeds long term.
Fentanyl and its derivatives account for about **one-third** of the roughly 60,000 yearly US opioid overdose deaths (the book’s figure)
Settles the **autonomic hyperactivity** of withdrawal (tachycardia, tremor, sweating); clonidine is the comparable α2 agonist in the book.

sideEffects.e: Can **precipitate withdrawal** in opioid-dependent patients (book states this for opioid antagonists generally)

pearls: Better at cutting **heavy drinking** (≥5 drinks/day men, ≥4 women) than at securing complete abstinence.
Patients who try to **drink or inject over** the blockade find it unrewarding, which helps extinguish the habit.
Combined with bupropion, approved for **obesity** (Ch 6 mention).

sideEffects.e: Can **precipitate withdrawal** in opioid-dependent patients (book states this for opioid antagonists generally)

pearls: Used in the Sinclair method as an **oral dose ~1 h before drinking**, as an alternative to naltrexone.
Targets the state after chronic alcohol is stopped: **glutamate overexcitation** (excitotoxicity) plus GABA deficiency.
**Detox and deprivation** do not abolish craving; cue-triggered craving can persist for years and deprivation may raise later drinking.
